patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a clear hamburger icon in the top-right corner, while the desktop sketch instead shows inline navigation items across the top.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close a mobile navigation panel or overlay containing the site links. The trigger should reflect open/closed state and likely hide page scrolling while the menu is open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a full-screen overlay, side drawer, or dropdown panel, nor whether it includes social links or secondary actions.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place navigation/header controls at the very top in a persistent-looking header area: hamburger on mobile and horizontal nav on desktop. This strongly implies the header remains available while scrolling through long content below.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header should remain fixed or become fixed on scroll so navigation stays accessible while the user moves through the image-and-text content. Active page indication may also need to persist in the nav.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show a scrolled state, so sticky behavior is inferred from the long-page layout rather than directly drawn.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches prominently feature image tiles/cards near the top of the content area. In portfolio/gallery layouts, large image blocks commonly imply click/tap-to-open enlarged media, especially when the page otherwise contains static descriptive text beneath.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Selecting an image should likely open it in an overlay/lightbox with dismiss behavior. If multiple images are part of a gallery, the modal may support previous/next navigation and background scroll lock.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw a lightbox, zoom icon, or arrows, so this is inferred from the gallery-style presentation and may alternatively be simple navigation to detail pages.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Any mobile hamburger menu overlay and any image modal/lightbox implied by the gallery blocks would require managed keyboard focus. Desktop also needs focus handling if image overlays open from the gallery.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu or image modal opens, focus should move into the opened component, remain constrained appropriately while open, and return to the triggering control when closed.
patterns_found.ambiguities: If the images navigate to separate pages instead of opening overlays, focus management would mainly apply to the mobile menu only.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict long vertically scrolling pages with substantial content below the fold, which commonly implies a return-to-top affordance for usability on content-heavy portfolio pages.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A back-to-top control could appear after the user scrolls down and smoothly return them to the top/header when activated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit button is drawn in the sketches, so this is speculative and based only on the long-scroll layout.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a relatively simple portfolio/content page with most interaction concentrated in navigation and media presentation rather than forms or complex widgets. Mobile clearly requires a hamburger-driven navigation pattern, while desktop uses exposed top-level navigation. Across both viewports, the large image blocks strongly suggest gallery interactions that may open in a modal/lightbox, which in turn introduces focus-management requirements. The long-scroll composition also makes sticky header behavior plausible and a back-to-top affordance possible, though the latter is less explicit in the drawings.
